title: Script-tag adm that document.writes static markup; inert, no network call

source.name: IAB OpenRTB 2.6 — Bid.adm ("ad markup"); document.write ad-tag pattern is a common real-world wire shape, not a spec object
source.notes: The document.write pattern itself is a widely-observed ad-tag idiom; the specific script and markup here are original, invented for this corpus.

modifications: All auction, bid, creative, site, app and publisher identifiers are synthetic.
All domains use reserved .test names; no real user IDs, IP addresses, consent strings or tracker endpoints.
All text and SVG artwork are original; no public creative copied.
device.ip is the documentation-only address 192.0.2.11; OS values describe a synthetic test device.

adm is a <script> element that calls document.write with a literal markup string; no external script src, no fetch/XHR, no navigation — deliberately inert so this case isolates the classify→execute path from any network concern.
provenance.sanitized: Only synthetic identifiers, original fixture creatives, reserved domains and TEST-NET addresses. No live tokens, subscriber IDs or real tracking URLs.

pairApplicability.note: Every response bid references an offered impression; auction identifiers match.

specNotes: Protocol validity is based on cited fields, not on current Core output. Optional-field warnings do not make this pair invalid.

The adm is markup by the classifier's own cheapest-honest-test (creative-classify.js MARKUP_SHAPE: an opening angle bracket) — a <script> element is markup, and the only kind that reaches an iframe srcdoc is markup, so this reaches the frame like any banner HTML.
The sandboxed frame is script-src 'unsafe-inline' with no external src allowed; this creative never attempts a network call, so no CSP refusal and no #creativeBlocked ledger entry is expected.
Browser assertions are proposed observables; this corpus has not been run in a browser.
Assert the fixture label text is visible in the DOM after document.write runs (not merely present in the raw adm string before script execution).
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.
